title: Together Compiler: continual compilation for AI inference
authors: Reyna Abhyankar, Dylan Lim, Simran Arora
gist: The technical description. Inputs are a traffic shape, a model and a chip. Parallel agents propose changes to the engine's forward pass and share findings on a message board. The enabling trick is infrastructure: an engine that stays up and hot-reloads candidates, in a fast tier with a few layers and a slow tier with the full model on real data, plus a cost model that prunes parallelism layouts.
changes: Shows that the investment is in the evaluation rig, not the agent. Cutting engine start-up from minutes to seconds is what makes hundreds of experiments affordable.
caveats: Says nothing about how output correctness is checked, how drift is detected, or how often recompilation runs. The companion paper concedes one headline comparison sets their 8-way parallel run against a published 4-way one. Page metadata says 3.7x where the text says 2.6x.

numbers.baseline: best published AgentX configurations of open engines

numbers.metric: Prompt length in one region's working hours

bears_on.note: Agent search in production on serverless endpoints, by their account.
A two-tier engine exists because timings on a few layers do not predict the full model on real data.
Prompt lengths rose about 80% in the two weeks after a model release. The target moves.
Claims a private lead of up to 2.6x over the best public configurations.
